priorFailure.disposition: The four profile directories reappeared after the earlier exact-argv drain. They were retained unchanged; that drain did not establish descendant exit.

diagnosis.privateLaunch: Disposable Chrome launched detached, creating a new session and process group whose ID was its PID. No live POC listener, port 7478, unrelated Chrome, or process group was signaled.
observations: A fresh launch had 12 same-UID private-session members before close. Chrome rewrote each command line into one space-containing field, so none contained --user-data-dir=<profile> as an exact argv element; three helper processes mentioned no profile path at all.

After Browser.close was acknowledged and the launched parent exited, one same-session non-zombie helper without a profile argument remained at the first scan and drained by 25 ms. The old exact-argv predicate would have reported no profile users during that interval.
diagnosis.safetyBoundary: The fix observes only the launched detached session's same-UID /proc members, including helpers in another process group within that session. It sends no process-group signal; SIGKILL remains limited to the launched child after the bounded close attempt. Unreadable or mismatched membership and a drain timeout retain the profile. Two consecutive empty scans are required before removal.
